title: Zero Digits Left: Every Story Speaks the Address First | vitalii.no
description:
Driving at night at speed, a flash story would start talking about a building without ever saying which one it was. Years and other numbers were written as plain digits, and the speech engine read them out wrong almost every time — so a listener had no reliable way to place the story or trust the numbers inside it.

New stories and chapters now open with the building's real address, looked up via Kartverket (Norway's official mapping registry) and spoken aloud in both Ukrainian and Norwegian before the flash begins. Every number inside the generated text is spelled out in words instead of left as digits for the voice engine to mangle. A new retroactive script walks the already-published catalog and applies the same fix, re-voicing only the chapters it actually touched rather than re-rendering everything from scratch.

The result: new stories are address-first and digit-free from the moment they're generated, and the existing catalog is being brought up to zero digits left to mishear — without a full re-voice of the chapters that didn't need it.
